message: The search starts at target + 1, so a target that is already a fast length (e.g. 8) is skipped and 9 is returned; it must start at target.
target == 0 is accepted (and returns 1) while scipy.fft.next_fast_len raises ValueError for non-positive targets; the check should be target < 1.
n / p is float division, so for lengths above 2**53 (e.g. 3**40) the factorization loses precision and fast lengths are misclassified; use integer division n //= p.
Remove the debug print to stdout.
prev_fast_len is added to _scipy_fft.__all__ and the README but not imported or listed in __all__ of the public scipy_fft module, so it is unavailable and not dispatched by __ua_function__.
The test only asserts n >= target, which passes with the off-by-one bug; assert the exact smallest fast length (and that fast targets map to themselves), and add tests for prev_fast_len.
A user-visible API addition needs a CHANGELOG.md entry under [dev] as CONTRIBUTING.md requires.
